title: Pollo alla Cacciatora
subtitle: Hunter's chicken braised with tomatoes, olives, and rosemary
excerpt: Pollo alla cacciatora is hunter's chicken: bone-in chicken pieces braised slowly in tomatoes, white wine, garlic, olives, and rosemary. It is one of the most widespread Italian braised chicken dishes, made in slightly different versions across Tuscany, Umbria, and Lazio. The combination of olives and rosemary gives it a distinctly earthy, Italian flavour.
sourceNotes: Pollo alla cacciatora (hunter's chicken) is one of the most widely made Italian chicken dishes. The name refers to the hunting tradition of cooking game birds and chicken with foraged herbs and whatever wine was available. The Tuscan and Umbrian versions typically include olives, capers, and rosemary.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the cooked chicken in its sauce. Reheat gently.

content.text: The key to cacciatora is browning the chicken properly before the braising liquid goes in. A pale, steamed chicken without a brown crust will produce a thin, pallid sauce. Take the time to brown each piece well on both sides. The olives go in at the end, not at the start -- they become bitter if cooked too long.

Heat {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} olive oil in a wide, heavy pan over medium-high heat. Season {{chicken-thigh}} chicken thighs with {{salt-table}} salt and {{black-pepper}} pepper. Brown well on both sides, about 5 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add {{onion}} onion to the pan and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Add {{garlic}} garlic and {{rosemary}} rosemary and cook for 1 minute. Pour in {{white-wine-dry}} wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes. Add {{tinned-tomatoes}} tomatoes and crush roughly.

Return the chicken to the pan. Cover and simmer over very low heat for 35 minutes. Add {{olives-green}} olives and {{capers}} capers and cook for a further 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce is thick. Taste for {{salt-table}} salt.

items.symptom: The sauce is thin and watery
items.cause: The chicken released too much liquid, or the lid was left on too tight.
items.fix: Remove the lid for the last 10 minutes and simmer over medium heat to reduce the sauce. Chicken thighs with bone in release less liquid than boneless -- use bone-in pieces.

content.text: Pollo alla cacciatora appears across central Italy in different regional forms. The Tuscan version is heavier on rosemary, capers, and olives; the Roman version uses peppers; the Umbrian version sometimes adds anchovies. All versions share the same technique: browned chicken pieces braised in tomatoes and wine. The name (hunter's chicken) suggests the dish was originally made with wild birds caught in the field and cooked over a camp fire with foraged herbs.
